answer: Before the horse is ever harnessed the saddler lays out his straps in a row and counts them twice. Proof of saddler harness via strap count is the saddler's rule: a harness the saddler stitches only after 13 straps are cut true, each strap oiled by the saddler himself. The pearl is the harness itself, pale as new leather. The inlet is the creek where the hides are washed. The spiral is the curl of the strap round the buckle. A forger must cut 13 straps true, stitch the harness and oil every buckle, and the trace still snaps at the first hill.
